li.label: Ask them to walk the colony's bounds tonight
li.tip: Two of the wardens walk up to the colony's gate at dusk and keep an eye on the road from there for a few hours. They like being asked.

outcomes.li: Two of the wardens came up to the gate at dusk with their spears and a lantern, and stood the colony's watch with it until the small hours.
{X_nameDef} sent two of the wardens up to the gate for the night watch. "Our road, your gate," {X_pronoun} said. "Same thing."

lines.li: Who goes there? Oh, the cat.

li.label: Pay them for keeping the road ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: Wardens are paid, where their people come from. Silver for the road they keep puts the colony in good standing with them, and with their people.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} carried {COUNT} silver down to the wardens' post. {X_nameDef} counted it, split it, and said {FACTION} would hear how the colony dealt with those who kept its road.
{X_nameDef} took the colony's silver with a nod. "We'd keep it anyway. This makes it a pleasure."

texts.li: {FACTION}'s road wardens have made camp {PLACE} to put up their post: {X_nameDef} and the others, with their spears stacked and a palisade already marked out with stakes.
The road wardens of {FACTION} have pitched camp {PLACE}, where the post is to go. {X_nameDef} walked the ground twice before letting anyone unpack.

settled.li: The wardens' camp {PLACE} has its fire going and its first palisade posts in. Someone is always at the road end of it, watching.
Smoke rises from the wardens' camp {PLACE}, and the sound of an axe. The post is going up.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the wardens camped {PLACE}, came to the gate at the end of {X_possessive} watch. "I've kept other people's roads long enough," {X_pronoun} said. "I'd keep this one as one of yours, if there's a place."

farewell.li: The wardens of {FACTION} have struck their camp {PLACE} and ridden back to their people. The half-built post stands empty.
{FACTION}'s wardens are gone from {PLACE}, called back down the road. {X_nameDef} said, at the gate: "Keep the road for us a while."

li.label: Ask them to stand guard while they're here
li.tip: They have fought before and would rather fight for a roof than run from one. From now on they take up arms against whatever threatens the colony while their camp stands, as a war party does.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} looked at the others, and the others looked at their boots, and then {X_pronoun} said yes. "We left a fight that wasn't ours. This one would be."
{A_nameDef} asked the deserters camped {PLACE} to stand guard, and {X_nameDef} laughed, not unkindly. "Soldiers again. All right. For you, and for the fire."

li.label: Give them silver for the road ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: They came away with their weapons and little else. Silver to go on with eases their stay and sends them off better than they came.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} carried {COUNT} silver over to the deserters' fire. {X_nameDef} turned it over in {X_possessive} hands a while before pocketing it. "Nobody's paid us in a season."
{X_nameDef} took the colony's silver and divided it four ways, exactly, as if on a parade ground.

li.label: Give them steel for their gear
li.refuseLabel: The colony's steel is its own

askTexts.li: {X_nameDef} came up from the deserters' camp {PLACE} with a cracked blade and a question. Their gear is a season past mending, and a little of the colony's steel would see it right. They'd work for it, {X_pronoun} says, if the colony likes.

[ws:war|ws:creed|ws:sellswords|ws:levy] The deserters camped {PLACE} came out of {SITUATION} with their weapons and nothing to keep them with. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few bars of steel to mend what they carry.

li.tip: Fifteen steel is carried out to their camp. They mend their gear by the fire, and remember whose steel it was.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} carried the steel down to the deserters' camp, and the sound of filing came up from it until dark. {X_nameDef} said, when {A_pronoun} left, that nobody had given them anything in a long while.

refused.li: {X_nameDef} nodded, as if {X_pronoun} had expected it, and went back to the camp to bind the blade with wire.

titles.li: Deserters at the edge of the land

texts.li: A handful of fighters of {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}, well out of sight of the road. {X_nameDef} says, without being asked, that they are done with soldiering. They ask only to rest a few days, and that nobody who comes asking after them is told.

[ws:war|ws:creed|ws:sellswords|ws:levy] {FACTION} sent them to fight in {SITUATION}, and they have come away from it: {X_nameDef} and a few others, armed still, hungry, and done. They have camped {PLACE} and asked {A_nameDef} for leave to stay a while, out of sight.

[lowtech] Spears and a dented shield lean against a tree {PLACE}, and the people who carried them have lit a small fire and sat down as if they didn't mean to get up again. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' rest on the colony's land, and no questions.

settled.li: The deserters' camp {PLACE} is small and hard to see from the road, which is how they want it. Someone is always awake.
The fighters camped {PLACE} have their weapons stacked within reach and their backs to a bank. They sleep in turns.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, from the deserters' camp {PLACE}, came to the gate without {X_possessive} weapon and asked whether the colony could use someone who knows how to hold a line and would rather never have to again.
{X_nameDef} has been splitting the colony's wood in the mornings without being asked. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether there might be a place here for good, for someone done with soldiering.

farewell.li: The deserters' camp {PLACE} is empty this morning, the fire cold. They went in the night, as people do who don't want to be followed.
{X_nameDef} and the others have gone on from {PLACE}, looking for somewhere nobody knows their faces. {X_nameDef} left a word of thanks at the gate.
[ws:war|ws:creed|ws:sellswords|ws:levy] The deserters have gone from {PLACE}, away from {SITUATION} and from everyone who was in it.
